item.title: The Bitter Lesson Comes for the Factory
item.dc:creator: Christopher Laing
item.description:
Every year or so, the people most serious about building software with AI settle on a new craft. First it was prompt engineering, then harness engineering, and now it is the agentic factory. Each was necessary in its moment, each delivered real gains to the people who mastered it, and each is falling to the same force: the Bitter Lesson.

What has changed is not the lesson but the speed at which it is taught. Frontier models are now improving quickly enough that the lesson is outpacing even the people most engaged with the state of the art, and nowhere more so than in software.

item.title: High-Code: The Unexpected Path to AI Democratisation
item.dc:creator: Christopher Laing
item.description: Years ago, I read a blog post called Always Bet on Text that left a lasting impression on me. Not only did it accord with my own experience, but it gave me a good, compact reference frame to think about technology. No recent technology is more suited to this reference frame than Generative AI, for the simple reason that, at its core, modern GenAI is all about text completion.

item.title: The Memo
item.dc:creator: Christopher Laing
item.description:
In 2002, Amazon’s Jeff Bezos issued a memo that has entered tech industry canon. The memo, known as the “API Mandate”, is generally perceived as being a statement about technology at Amazon, and is therefore widely admired by technologists and wholly ignored by executives. This is unfortunate, because it’s no exaggeration to say that the API Mandate completely transformed Amazon as a business and laid the foundation for its success. Better still, unlike many things that global technology titans do, it is something that can be replicated and put to use by almost any business.

In this post, we’ll talk about the memo, and how it created the systems and incentives for radical organisational transformation.

item.title: The Business Implications of Combinatorial Optimisation by Deep Learning
item.dc:creator: Christopher Laing
item.description: Recently, Deep Learning has revolutionised a multitude of technical fields, most notably Computer Vision and Natural Language Processing. The implications for business are enormous, with the ramifications of these change still filtering through the mostly technology-shy world of business. There are signs that Combinatorial Optimisation might be the next technical field to undergo Revolution-By-Neural-Network. If this comes to fruition, then the impact on business will be seismic.
